findings.issue: The SPEC-09 Soft clause ('only Calling station and Rock replacements') is checked over a 300-hand seed-42 run that produces very few replacements (the builder notes one), so a playtest-path bug that drew Soft replacements from the wrong set could pass by luck.
findings.evidence: `const soft = replacements(run('Soft').hands); expect(soft.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. The style set itself is pinned by the 10,000-draw tallies in tests/bots/replacement.acceptance.test.ts, and the runner calls the same drawReplacementStyle, so the practical risk is low.
findings.fix: Also assert each Soft replacement's style equals drawReplacementStyle('Soft', 6, handReplayCode(42, hand-1), seat), as the Mixed loop already does. That pins the preset the runner passes in, whatever the draw count.

findings.issue: The helper `withFinalStacks(stacks, table = KINGS_SHOWDOWN)` is defined twice in new code (here and tests/table/next-hand.test.ts:100), and a narrower copy already exists at tests/table/next-hand.acceptance.test.ts:41. The spec's reuse list names the `withFinalStacks` pattern and tests/support/table-scenarios.ts.
findings.evidence: The bodies are identical at tests/table/replace-bot.acceptance.test.ts:18-24 and tests/table/next-hand.test.ts:100-106.
findings.fix: Export one `withFinalStacks(stacks, table = KINGS_SHOWDOWN)` from tests/support/table-scenarios.ts and import it in both new or unlocked files. Leave the locked file alone.

findings.issue: Spec section 11 says the Q-4 unlock of tests/playtest/policy-lineup.acceptance.test.ts is recorded under TASK-1.52, but no unlock event exists there. TASK-3.4 has one for next-hand.acceptance. test-integrity still passes for TASK-1.52, because the file is not in its locked_tests (only e2e/worker-delay.spec.ts is) and its assertion count is unchanged.
findings.evidence: TASK-1.52's locked_tests keys are ['e2e/worker-delay.spec.ts'], and its state has no unlock event that mentions policy-lineup. The edit itself is exactly as approved: 200 becomes 45 in three places, and both toEqual and not.toEqual are kept.
findings.fix: Record the approved change in the audit trail (doit.py unlock TASK-1.52 tests/playtest/policy-lineup.acceptance.test.ts --reason 'TASK-6.8 Q-4 ...'), or have the docs stage note that the file was never hard-locked.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Every SPEC item behaves as specified. In cash, nextHand replaces a $0 bot with the next unused replacement name, a style drawn from replacementGenerator(code, seat) over config.lineUp's styles, and buyIn(stake)=$160. A bot with $1 or more keeps its stack. The user seat and sit-and-go keep the TEMPORARY line. Several busts in one hand go in ascending seat order through hand.players. The A-6 RangeError is in place. The recorded deviation (drawReplacementStyle in src/table/session.ts) is justified: tests/bots/tag.test.ts:147 forbids engine runtime imports under src/bots, and the function is pure and exported as specified. Allowed styles come from seatLineUp, with MIXED_CYCLE order and Custom giving all four, and nextIntUnbiased gives a uniform draw. The position only ever increases, so names are never reused, including 'Jay 2' after Zed. Mutation checks in a scratch copy: (1) replay ignoring --styles for policies and (2) the runner keeping preset policies after a replacement both make the SPEC-12 acceptance test fail, so the replay check has real power. The locked edits match Q-4: next-hand.acceptance lines 93-96 and the 60-hand loop (a $0 bot gets a new name and 160, the user below 96 gets 160, an unchanged stack means an unchanged seat, and the hand-43 seat-2 bot carries $94), and policy-lineup goes from 200 to 45 hands with both comparisons kept. test-integrity passes for TASK-6.8, TASK-3.4 and TASK-1.52; the TASK-3.4 warnings are older files this task did not touch. The default playtest SHA is still aacd5e94...e01. The app adds no crypto draw: nextHand is pure and the UI is unchanged. Unit coverage is 100% lines for session.ts, lineup.ts and bot-random.ts. The slowest new test takes 2.3 s, and the 10,000-hand run sits behind TLH_SLOW_TESTS and test:slow. The size over budget (997 lines, 16 files) is mostly tests and the approved --styles surface, and I found no scope creep.
